text.title: Ayush Pavilion Wins Gold Medal at IITF 2026

text.title: Breakthrough in Tunnel-14 of Rishikesh-Karnaprayag Rail Project
text.one_liner: Indian Railways achieved the main tunnel breakthrough of the 6.59 km long Tunnel-14 in Uttarakhand's Rudraprayag district.
text.summary: Indian Railways successfully achieved the main tunnel breakthrough of Tunnel-14, measuring 6.59 km, in the Rishikesh-Karnaprayag Rail Project located in Uttarakhand's Rudraprayag district. The excavation connected the 4.7 km section from Portal-1 in Sumerpur and 1.79 km from Portal-2 in Marora. Specialized techniques like pre-excavation, multi-drifting, micropiles, and controlled daytime blasting were utilized to ensure safety under inhabited areas.
key_points: Project: Rishikesh-Karnaprayag Rail Project.
Tunnel length: 6.59 km (Tunnel-14).
Location: Rudraprayag district, Uttarakhand.
Connects Portal-1 (Sumerpur) and Portal-2 (Marora).

mcqs.explanation: Tunnel-14 is part of the strategically important Rishikesh-Karnaprayag Rail Project in Uttarakhand.

text.title: BSL-3 Facility Inaugurated at CSIR-CDRI Lucknow
text.one_liner: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh inaugurated the BSL-3/ABSL-3 facility and Dr. B. Mukerji Lecture Theatre at CSIR-CDRI, Lucknow.
text.summary: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh inaugurated the state-of-the-art Biosafety Level-3 (BSL-3)/Animal Biosafety Level-3 (ABSL-3) facility and Dr. B. Mukerji Lecture Theatre at CSIR-Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. The facility will strengthen high-containment research on Mycobacterium tuberculosis and other infectious diseases. CSIR-CDRI has developed 13 marketed drugs, filed over 1,000 patents, and licensed more than 80 process technologies.

Focus areas: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and challenging infectious diseases.
CDRI achievements: Developed 13 marketed drugs, licensed over 80 process technologies, and filed over 1,000 patents.
Notable CDRI contraceptive drug: Centchroman (Ormeloxifene).

text.title: CSIR-CRRI Wins CII 4R Awards 2026 for Waste Technology
text.one_liner: CSIR-CRRI won the CII 4R Awards 2026 and was recognized among India's Top 30 Waste-to-Worth Leaders for its Steel Slag Road Technology.

text.title: New technology developed for stable, tunable and scalable white LEDs
text.one_liner: Researchers developed a dual-protection strategy using halide perovskite nanocrystals to create stable, tunable white LEDs.
text.summary: Researchers from CeNS Bengaluru and IIT Delhi have developed an innovative dual-protection strategy to prevent colour blurring in halide perovskite nanocrystals used for white LEDs. By reducing halide vacancies with lead selenide and applying a 5 to 6 nanometre thick atomic layer deposition of aluminum oxide, they successfully stabilised white light emission. This technology enables flexible, cost-effective white-lighting technologies for smartphones and lighting.
key_points: Developed by researchers from CeNS Bengaluru and IIT Delhi.
Uses halide perovskite nanocrystals with formula CsPbX3.
Employs lead selenide treatment and aluminium oxide atomic layer deposition encapsulation.
Published in the scientific journal Small.

mcqs.explanation: Researchers reduced halide vacancies on the crystal surface using a material called lead selenide.

mcqs.explanation: The text states the chemical formula is CsPbX3, where X can be chlorine, bromine, or iodine.

text.title: NBA Disburses ₹13.76 Crore in ABS Funds for Biodiversity Conservation
text.one_liner: The National Biodiversity Authority disbursed ₹13.76 crore across 28 states and 4 UTs under the ABS mechanism.
text.summary: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) disbursed ₹13.76 crore to 28 states and 4 union territories to promote biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of biological resources. The funds originate from Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) contributions by AYUSH manufacturing companies utilising medicinal plants. Among medicinal plants, species like Guggul, Ashwagandha, and Bhringraj contributed majorly to the benefit-sharing amount.

Total utilization covered 234 plant species.

text.title: NABARD's State Rural Development Conclave in Rajasthan
text.one_liner: NABARD hosted the State Rural Development Conclave 2026-27 in Jaipur, estimating Rajasthan's priority-sector credit potential at ₹5.76 lakh crore for 2027-28.
text.summary: NABARD's Rajasthan Regional Office organised the State Rural Development Conclave 2026-27 at Jaipur, bringing together policymakers, bankers, and grassroots institutions. NABARD's Chief General Manager Dr. R. Ravibabu estimated the State's priority-sector credit potential for 2027-28 at ₹5.76 lakh crore. Chief Secretary Shri V. Srinivas highlighted key initiatives like PM KUSUM and water security projects. Four technical sessions were conducted, and various successful rural groups were felicitated.

Priority-sector credit potential for 2027-28 estimated at ₹5.76 lakh crore.

text.title: RBI Issues Amendment Directions on Suspected Money Mule Accounts
text.one_liner: RBI issued KYC amendment directions to establish a Standard Operating Procedure for placing temporary debit holds on suspected money mule accounts.
text.summary: Following stakeholder feedback on draft directions issued on September 11, 2026, the Reserve Bank of India issued final Amendment Directions concerning suspected money mule accounts to prevent cyber-enabled financial frauds. The directions lay down a uniform, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) allowing banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on accounts linked to fraud and to remove them in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies. The directions come into effect from July 1, 2027, or earlier at a bank's discretion.
key_points: Draft directions were initially issued on September 11, 2026, for stakeholder feedback.
Introduces an SOP for banks to place temporary debit holds on suspected money mule and cyber fraud accounts.
Holds will be managed and removed in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs).
Directions become effective from July 1, 2027, or an earlier date chosen by the bank.

text.title: 31st Meeting of SAC to Review MSME Credit Flow Held in Kolkata
text.one_liner: RBI Deputy Governor chaired the 31st Standing Advisory Committee meeting in Kolkata to review credit flow to MSMEs.
text.summary: The 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee to review credit flow to MSMEs took place in Kolkata on November 27, 2026, chaired by RBI Deputy Governor Shri Swaminathan J. Participants included senior officials from the Ministry of MSME, Ministry of Finance, SIDBI, NABARD, and other financial institutions. Discussions focused on collateral-free lending, cash-flow-based lending using ULI, TReDS invoice settlements, and MSMED (Amendment) Act provisions.

text.title: RBI Announces Auction of 91-Day, 182-Day and 364-Day Treasury Bills
text.one_liner: RBI announced an auction for 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day Treasury Bills totalling ₹23,000 crore on December 02, 2026.
text.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced the auction of Government of India Treasury Bills worth a total notified amount of ₹23,000 crore, comprising 91-Day (₹8,000 crore), 182-Day (₹8,000 crore), and 364-Day (₹7,000 crore) bills. The auction will be held on December 02, 2026, using the multiple price method on the E-Kuber system. Retail investors can participate through the Retail Direct portal with allocation restricted to a maximum of 5 percent of the notified amount.
key_points: Total Notified Amount: ₹23,000 crore
Auction Date: December 02, 2026
Settlement Date: December 03, 2026
Retail Investor Limit: Maximum 5 percent of the notified amount
